claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy has a single-phase BCC dendritic microstructure.
The initial TiVNbTa alloy is produced by mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering.
Reported TiVNbTa has a yield strength of about 330 MPa at 1273 K.
Reported TiVNbTa has a compressive strength of 423 MPa at 1273 K.
Internal oxidation during powder consolidation followed by an oxidation anneal can introduce nanometer-scale Y2O3 particles into TiVNbTa.
The proposed processing route will produce a uniform dispersion of Y2O3 nanoparticles in the BCC matrix.
The dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles will remain thermally stable under the applicable high-temperature conditions.
Y2O3 nanoparticles will hinder dislocation motion in TiVNbTa.
Y2O3 nanoparticles will suppress grain-boundary migration in TiVNbTa.
Suppressing grain-boundary migration will retard microstructural coarsening and high-temperature softening.
Y2O3 dispersion strengthening will raise the TiVNbTa yield strength at 1273 K from about 330 MPa to more than 450 MPa.
The intervention will maintain compressive strength at a level compatible with use as a heat-transfer interlayer between tungsten and CuCrZr.
The intervention will maintain ductility at a level compatible with use as a heat-transfer interlayer between tungsten and CuCrZr.
The applicable thermal condition is 1273 K.
The applicable mechanical condition is compressive loading to 30% strain.
The magnitude of strengthening depends on obtaining a uniform oxide dispersion without disrupting BCC phase stability.
Oxygen partial pressure and annealing duration are critical process variables for the proposed strengthening response.
